title: Multi-Modal, Multi-Temporal Geospatial Foundation Models Improve Global Above-Ground Biomass Estimation
abstract: arXiv:2608.04792v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Accurate estimation of above-ground biomass (AGB) from satellite imagery is essential for the large-scale monitoring of carbon stocks, yet it remains a challenging regression task at global scale. Geospatial Foundation Models (GFMs) have recently emerged as a promising machine learning paradigm to derive general-purpose representations from Earth observation (EO) data, but their utility for quantitative regression tasks like biomass estimation remains largely unexplored, as most benchmarks focus on classification and segmentation. Here, we benchmark 13 GFMs for above-ground biomass estimation, specifically GEDI L4A biomass values. We compare them against a fully supervised state-of-the-art (SOTA) baseline trained on A Global-scale Biomass Dataset (AGBD), a machine learning-ready benchmark spanning diverse biomes and geographies. translated_title: 多模态、多时相地理空间基础模型改进全球地上生物量估计
translated_abstract: 从卫星影像中准确估计地上生物量（AGB）对于大尺度的碳储量监测至关重要，但在全球尺度上这仍然是一项具有挑战性的回归任务。地理空间基础模型（GFMs）近来作为一种有前景的机器学习范式出现，能够从地球观测（EO）数据中提取通用表示，但它们在生物量估计等定量回归任务中的效用尚未被充分探索，因为大多数基准测试集中于分类和分割任务。本文对13个地理空间基础模型在地面生物量估计任务上进行了基准测试，具体使用GEDI L4A生物量值。我们将它们与在AGBD（A Global-scale Biomass Dataset，一个覆盖多种生物群落和地理区域的机器学习就绪基准数据集）上训练的全监督最先进（SOTA）基线进行比较。所评估的大多数地理空间基础模型相较于监督基线表现明显不佳，无论是……（原文截断）
tldr: 本文对13个地理空间基础模型在全球地上生物量估计任务上进行了系统性基准测试，发现多模态、多时相的地理空间基础模型能够超越全监督基线方法，从而改进全球地上生物量的估计。
en_tdlr: This paper benchmarks 13 geospatial foundation models on global above-ground biomass estimation, demonstrating that multi-modal, multi-temporal GFMs outperform fully supervised baselines and improve global AGB estimation.
